_help: Locked 30-day starter plan rendered by start-here.html. Reader-relative: day 1 is whatever calendar day the reader picks the plan up. Editing label values changes which chapter day-N points to; editing note text adjusts the pastoral framing. Day 1 must remain John 1 and day 30 must remain 2 Timothy 3 to satisfy the spec's locked starter list (Requirement 10.2).

entries.label: John 1
entries.note: John starts before the beginning. This is who Jesus has always been — the Word, the light, God with us.

entries.label: John 3
entries.note: A teacher comes to Jesus by night and gets the most famous verse in the Bible. Read it slowly; this is the heart of the gospel.

entries.label: John 8
entries.note: A woman is dragged in to be condemned. Watch how Jesus answers — both her accusers and her — and you'll see what mercy looks like.

entries.label: John 14
entries.note: Jesus is preparing his friends for what comes next. 'I am the way' is not a slogan here; it's a promise to people about to be left behind.

entries.label: Mark 1
entries.note: Mark moves fast. In one chapter Jesus is announced, baptized, tested, calls his first followers, and starts healing people. Keep up.

entries.label: Mark 4
entries.note: Three short stories about how the kingdom grows, then a storm. The same Jesus who tells the parables also tells the wind to be quiet.

entries.label: Mark 8
entries.note: Halfway through Mark, Jesus asks the question the whole gospel is built on: 'Who do you say I am?' Sit with your own answer.

entries.label: Psalm 23
entries.note: The most-read poem in human history. Read it as if you wrote it about your own life — because in a real way, you can.

entries.label: Psalm 51
entries.note: David has just done something terrible and he is not pretending otherwise. This is what real repentance sounds like, in front of a real God.

entries.label: Psalm 91
entries.note: A psalm for fear. When you don't know what's coming, this one tells you who is already there.

entries.label: Psalm 139
entries.note: You are known. Not generally — specifically, completely, before you said a single word. Let that land before you read tomorrow's chapter.

entries.label: Genesis 1
entries.note: Before there was anything, there was God, and his first move was to make. Creation is not an accident; it's a gift with your name on it.

entries.label: Genesis 3
entries.note: How everything broke. Notice that even in the middle of the disaster, God is still the one looking for the people, not the other way around.

entries.label: Exodus 3
entries.note: A bush on fire that doesn't burn up, and a name God gives himself: 'I AM.' He sees the suffering of his people and he is sending help.

entries.label: Romans 3
entries.note: Paul stops the conversation to make sure no one misunderstands: nobody earns this. Salvation is a gift, received by trust, period.

entries.label: Romans 5
entries.note: Reconciliation is the word. Not 'tolerance,' not 'second chance' — reconciliation. You and God on the same side again, because of Jesus.

entries.label: Romans 8
entries.note: Read the last paragraph out loud. Then read it again. Nothing — nothing — can separate you from the love of God in Christ Jesus.

entries.label: Romans 12
entries.note: Now what? Paul turns from theology to life. 'Be transformed by the renewing of your mind' is the bridge from believing to living.

entries.label: Isaiah 53
entries.note: Written 700 years before Jesus, this is a portrait of the cross. Read it knowing whose face is being described.

entries.label: Ephesians 2
entries.note: 'Dead in trespasses' to 'seated with him.' That's the journey of salvation in two prepositions. By grace, through faith.

entries.label: Galatians 3
entries.note: Paul is in arguing-with-friends mode here. The point: rules don't save anyone. Faith in Jesus does, and that has been the plan all along.

entries.label: James 1
entries.note: James is practical to the bone. If your faith doesn't show up in how you treat people and what you do with your tongue, he wants to know why.

entries.label: 1 John 4
entries.note: 'God is love' is not a sentiment here; it's a definition. And the test of whether we know him is whether that love is showing up in us.

entries.label: Matthew 5
entries.note: The Sermon on the Mount opens with the people Jesus calls blessed. This is the new shape of a life that follows him.

entries.label: Matthew 6
entries.note: How to give, how to pray, how to handle worry. Notice how often Jesus says 'your Father' — this is a family conversation, not a performance review.

entries.label: Matthew 7
entries.note: Three years of Jesus' teaching distilled into one chapter ending. 'Ask, seek, knock' is the invitation; the wise builder is the warning.

entries.label: Acts 2
entries.note: The first day of the church, and it does not look like a building. It looks like the Spirit poured out and ordinary people learning to live in common.

entries.label: Philippians 4
entries.note: Paul writes this from a prison cell and tells you not to be anxious. Read it knowing the man writing has earned the right to say so.

entries.label: 1 Corinthians 13
entries.note: The love chapter. Read it once for what it says about love. Read it again knowing every line is a description of Jesus.

entries.label: 2 Timothy 3
entries.note: Paul's last letter. He tells Timothy why Scripture matters and what to do with it. After 30 days, this is your invitation forward.
